ideas.title: ES noise-band intraday momentum on half-hour bars (Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon 'Beat the Market'), long card + short card
ideas.effect: When price is further from the open than it usually is at that time of day, and on the right side of VWAP, the move tends to keep going into the close (the 'noise area' break). Trend-following with a fat right tail.
ideas.evidence: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (SSRN 4824172, v. Feb 2025), SPY 2007 to Apr 2024, net of $0.0035/sh + $0.001 slippage: Sharpe 1.33, 19.6%/yr, beta slightly below 0. It takes 1.3-1.8 trades a day, decides only at :00/:30, and has a daily hit rate of 37-53%. Per year in their updated table (vol-targeted, up to 4x): 2020 +26.8%, 2021 +34.8%, 2022 +24.4%, 2023 +37.2%, 2024 +32.2%. It lost in 2016 (-12.8%) and 2017 (-6.9%). Sharpe is about 3.5 when VIX > 40, and Wednesday (FOMC days) is the strongest weekday. Related: Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens (JFE 2021): 17 equity-index futures 1974-2020 show intraday momentum, and the out-of-sample R2 is positive in 14 of 17. Decay: Rosa (cited in the paper) finds the first-half-hour to last-half-hour version weakened after 2013, but the noise-band version shows no decay through 2024.
ideas.family_mapping: noise_band; market ES (NQ as neighbor); bar 30 min (the paper's half-hour decision grid); group NY = nyam+mid+pm; fixed anchor=rth; main k = 0.25 / 0.35 / 0.5 (x daily ATR14). k 0.25-0.5 roughly brackets the paper's time-of-day noise width from 10:00 to 15:30. Two cards: dir long and dir short. The VWAP hunt only runs noise_band on 5 min, so this 30-min ES version does not duplicate it.
ideas.per_day: ~0.5-0.9 per side, ~1-1.5 for both cards on ES
ideas.needs_new_block: Optional, for a faithful version: a time-of-day band. That is the 14-day mean of |close(HH:MM)/open - 1| for each clock time, with the band anchored at max/min(09:30 open, prior 16:00 close) to adjust for gaps. The engine's flat k x daily ATR band is too wide early in the day and too narrow late.
ideas.risk: The paper's edge comes from a trailing exit (VWAP / band) that lets trend days run. The hm40 table caps targets at 2x the stop, so look at the 2x-target and wide-stop cells, and judge the average box, not the best one. Local results are mixed: noise_pm_long failed its drawdown limit and nq_noise_nyam_short lost money. The one locally confirmed pass is NQ midday long (idea 2).

ideas.title: Volatility-conditioned intraday momentum: noise band only on high-ATR-rank days
ideas.effect: Intraday time-series momentum is markedly stronger on volatile, high-volume and news days, so gate the momentum entry by the volatility regime.
ideas.evidence: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018, SPY 1993-2013): predictability is stronger on more volatile days, higher-volume days and macro-news days. Zarattini et al. 2024: Sharpe about 1.5 with VIX > 6 and about 3.5 with VIX > 40. Li, Sakkas & Urquhart (J. Financial Markets 2022, 16 developed markets): intraday time-series momentum is significant in and out of sample in most markets and stronger when liquidity is low and volatility is high. Jin, Kearney, Li & Yang (JFM 2020): in metals futures, high-volume / high-volatility first sessions show the strongest intraday momentum. Decay: none reported for the conditional effect, but the local last-30-minute test found big-move days did NOT beat all days on ES/NQ 2021-24, so this conditioning is unproven locally.
ideas.family_mapping: noise_band; NQ (ES neighbor); bar 5; group NY; fixed anchor=rth, k=0.3; main = open-layer gate=atr_rank, g_side with, g_lvl = 3 cutoffs (e.g. the 50th / 65th / 80th percentile on the engine's atr_rank scale), g_n 14. One side per card (long and short cards).
ideas.per_day: ~0.3-0.5 per side
ideas.needs_new_block: no (check the atr_rank scale and whether it ranks the intraday or the daily ATR)
ideas.risk: Overlaps with idea 1 (same entry family), so they are not independent trades. Higher cutoffs cut the trade count fast. VIX itself is not a gate here, and ATR rank is only a proxy.

ideas.title: GC US-hours down-drift: short gold at the COMEX day open, hold up to 3 h
ideas.effect: Gold's returns accrue overnight (Asia/Europe), and the US day session is on average negative: 'price too high at the open'.
ideas.evidence: Blose, Gondhalekar & Kort (J. Economics & Finance 2018): overnight returns are significantly positive and day returns significantly negative in COMEX gold front futures, the London Fix, gold miners and gold funds, and the result is economically meaningful after transaction costs. Post-2020 it has not decayed; it looks stronger. World Gold Council H1 2026 data (via Caixin/FXStreet): Asian hours +13% vs US hours -15% through 2026-06-26, with pullbacks mostly in US hours and rebounds in Asian hours. A counter-check found (falsifylab 2026, XAU 15 min 2018-2026) that 'London momentum' and 'Asia fade' rules on gold failed their holdout, so the edge is the session drift, not intraday patterns.
ideas.family_mapping: tod_drift; GC; bar 30 (6 bars = 3 h time exit); session pre (08:25 start, the COMEX pit-open area) with nyam as neighbor; card dir short; main off_min = 0 / 30 / 60.
ideas.per_day: ~1 (one per day)
ideas.risk: The engine labels tod_drift 'WEAK RATIONALE'. It must beat the same-side random pool (P4.2s), because a pure clock short in a gold bull market is a regime bet. The 2024-26 asymmetry is tied to Asian ETF/central-bank buying and can flip. 2026 months are out-of-sample in the blocks. Cost is $24 a trade vs an average 3-h move of about $1,000+, which is fine.

ideas.title: GC Asian-open up-drift: long gold from the Tokyo/Shanghai open, hold up to 3 h
ideas.effect: Mirror of idea 4: gold's gains concentrate in Asian trading hours (Shanghai/Tokyo physical and ETF demand).
ideas.evidence: Same sources as idea 4: Blose et al. 2018 (overnight positive) and WGC H1 2026 (Asian hours +13% while US hours -15%; 'Asia the engine of price support'). Chinese bar/coin demand was at a 12-year high in 2025 (WGC via FXStreet). CME: Asian hours were ~42% of micro-gold volume in Q2 2025, so liquidity is adequate. Decay: strengthened after 2020.
ideas.family_mapping: tod_drift; GC; bar 30; session eve (18:00 start, the evening before the trade date); card dir long; main off_min = 60 / 120 / 180 (19:00 / 20:00 / 21:00 ET, i.e. Tokyo open and Shanghai SGE night/day opens, depending on DST). Neighbor: session asia (00:00) off_min 0/30/60.
ideas.risk: Same regime risk as idea 4, and the two legs together are one bet on Asian gold demand. The eve session is 'Desk hosts evening sessions, shadow only', so check it can be traded live on the accounts. Thin overnight books: 1-tick slippage may be optimistic on stops.

ideas.title: Opening overreaction fade: large first-90-minute moves away from the 09:29 close revert
ideas.effect: Large moves at the open overshoot, and price snaps back toward the pre-open reference, more so after big up moves.
ideas.evidence: Grant, Wolf & Yu (J. Banking & Finance 2005), S&P 500 futures Nov 1987-Sep 2002: highly significant intraday reversals after large opening moves, stronger after large positive moves, but significance falls sharply after bid-ask costs. Fung, Mok & Lam (JBF 2000), S&P and Hang Seng futures: reversals grow with the size of the initial move and stay modestly profitable after costs. Yu, Rentzler & Wolf (JOIM 2005), NQ futures: the overnight return is mostly followed by reversal in the opening hours. Post-2020: Mesfin (arXiv 2605.04004, MNQ 5 min Dec 2021-Aug 2025) found expansion bars reverse right after their close (T -11.5 at bar+1, Asia session). The move is 'inside the bar', which supports fading, not following. The VVG study found reversal dominated in 2022-23 and continuation in 2024.
ideas.family_mapping: open_fade; NQ (ES neighbor); bar 1 (5 neighbor); session nyam (09:30-11:00, up to 3 trades); main k = 0.75 / 1.0 / 1.5 (x ATR30). Both sides in one card (it fades either way). The structure stop is the extreme.
ideas.risk: The academic samples are pre-2003 and gross of realistic costs. The reversal/continuation balance flips with the macro regime (Mesfin VVG). It fights idea 1 on trend days, so expect negative correlation, which is good for a portfolio but each leg must stand alone.

ideas.title: Late-morning reversal of an outsized 09:30-11:00 move (mid_fade)
ideas.effect: Morning moves are information-driven, while midday and afternoon flows are liquidity-driven and partly reverse an outsized morning move.
ideas.evidence: Xu (2017, US stocks 1993-2014, via CXO): intraday momentum is a morning effect and reversal an afternoon effect, and both halved between 1993-2003 and 2004-2014. In the local ledger (2026-09-20, ES/NQ 2021-08 to 2024-12), the strongest cell of the last-30 test was a REVERSAL: ES, prior close to 09:59 big move (|move| >= 0.5 ATR) vs the 15:30-16:00 return, t -2.97. Gao/Baltussen predict continuation into the last 30 minutes instead, so the literature conflicts. This is the weakest-evidence leg.
ideas.family_mapping: mid_fade; ES (NQ neighbor); bar 5; session mid; main k = 0.3 / 0.45 / 0.6 (|09:30 open to 11:00 close| >= k x daily ATR14), fading at the first mid close. Both sides in one card.
ideas.risk: The local reversal reading came from a window already read 3x. It conflicts with market intraday momentum, and the regime flips. Treat it as a diversifier, not a core leg.

ideas.title: Up-gap fade on volatile days (short card)
ideas.effect: The overnight return tends to reverse during the day session, mostly after up-gaps and when volatility is elevated.
ideas.evidence: Della Corte, Kosowski & Wang (2015): overnight-to-intraday reversal is the strongest short-term reversal in US stocks 1993-2014, consistent but much weaker in futures 1982-2014. Yu, Rentzler & Wolf (2005): NQ overnight return is associated with reversals. Grant-Wolf-Yu: overreaction is stronger after large positive opening moves. Recent: a practitioner test (falsifylab 2026, SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA hourly, ~2 years) of a gap fade gated by VIX z > 0.5 got Sharpe ~1.1 (0.96 after 4bp), with the edge concentrated in up-gap fades and negative at low VIX. Against it, Mesfin MNQ 2022-25 found an unconditional gap-fill fade at 09:30 / 09:45 / 10:00 null (gross about 0). Without a volatility gate it is dead.
ideas.family_mapping: gap; NQ (ES neighbor); bar 5; session nyam; fixed mode=fill, gate=atr_rank g_side with g_lvl = high cutoff; card dir short (= up-gap fade); main min_gap_atr = 0.15 / 0.3 / 0.5. Note: in fill mode the target is the prior close (tgt_r unused), so only the stop column of the heat map varies.
ideas.needs_new_block: no (a VIX-level gate would be truer than atr_rank)
ideas.risk: Low frequency. The unconditional version is null on MNQ 2022-25. The evidence for the gated version is one short practitioner sample. The fixed-target column does not apply in fill mode, so check that the hm40 grid accepts it.

ideas.title: Volume-confirmed 5-minute opening drive (ORB 'stocks in play' logic on the index)
ideas.effect: The first 5-minute candle's direction carries information, and more so when that candle trades on abnormally high volume for its clock window.
ideas.evidence: Zarattini & Aziz (SSRN 4416622, QQQ 2016-2023): 5-min ORB following the first candle's color, +0.13R a trade gross, hit rate 24% (10R target / EOD exit). Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz (2024): restricting ORB to high-relative-volume 'stocks in play' greatly improves it (cross-section of stocks). Gao et al.: momentum is stronger on high-volume days. Replications: NQ CFD 2015-2026 gross +0.131R (t 2.9) but about +0.06R for 2021-26 and about 0 net of CFD spread. Mesfin MNQ walk-forward: ORB long with a 75-min hold, net +2.82 pts after a 2-pt friction (gross ~4.8), T 0.88, years +2.4 / +7.0 / +15.1. The owner's NQ friction is only ~0.7 pt ($14), well below those cost assumptions. Against it, volume spikes and dry-ups alone are null on MNQ (Mesfin).
ideas.family_mapping: win_candle; NQ (ES neighbor); bar 5; session nyam; fixed start=09:30, mode=follow; main vol_m = 1.5 / 2 / 3 (candle volume vs the median of the same clock window). Both colors in one card, or long and short cards.
ideas.needs_new_block: Maybe. The 2026-10-20 hunt flagged candle930's vol_m / med_m as reading past sessions through the build seal (not walk-forward-safe). Confirm win_candle's vol_m is fixed before running.
ideas.risk: The 09:30 candle is heavily burned locally (many 09:30 candle / ORB variants lost on build days). The published edge lives at 10R targets, which the hm40 2x cap cuts off. Lowest prior of the list after idea 7.

lessons: Academic intraday edges on index futures are small. In Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens (JFE 2021, 60+ futures 1974-2020) the last-30-min timing strategy wins on 55% of days (equity futures, gross; Sharpe 1.73 at the asset-class level). That clears break-even+3 at 1:1 only if costs are <~0.03R. NQ at $14 (~0.7 pt) a trade on a 25-pt stop is ~0.03R, so the margin is thin.

Gold intraday momentum into the COMEX pit close (08:20-13:30) is real but tiny: R2 0.25%, out-of-sample R2 0.08% (Baltussen Table B3). It is too small to beat GC's $24 a trade. Do not build a GC last-30 leg.

Last-half-hour momentum (Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 2018; Baltussen 2021) did NOT replicate locally. ES/NQ 2021-08 to 2024-12 (ledger 2026-09-20): 12/12 cells negative, only 2022 green, and big-move days no better. The window has been read 3x. Supporting signs of decay: Rosa (post-2013 decline), 0DTE dealer gamma mostly positive (Dim-Eraker-Vilkov 2024; Princeton thesis 2026), and IBKR finding no rise in last-hour moves.

Missing block, if the owner still wants the Gao/Baltussen test: nothing enters at a clock time in the direction of the day's move so far (tod_drift is one-sided). The nearest proxy is noise_band with w_start ~15:25 and a small k, one card per side.

The European-open overnight drift in ES/NQ/YM (2-3 a.m. ET, ~3.7%/yr 1998-2019; Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan RFS 2023) has averaged ~0 since 2021 (NY Fed Liberty Street, July 2026). Do not build an overnight long leg on it.

The one published intraday-momentum family with strong 2020-2024 numbers is the Zarattini noise band (SPY +26.8 / +34.8 / +24.4 / +37.2 / +32.2% for 2020-24, net). Its edge is the right tail: hit rate 37-53% with a trailing VWAP/band exit. The hm40 targets (<= 2x stop) can truncate it, so read the 2x and wide-stop cells and judge the average box.

VWAP trend-following (Zarattini-Aziz QQQ 2018-23, Sharpe 2.1) runs at about a 17% hit rate and a 5.5 payoff ratio with ~6 round trips a day. Independent QuantConnect replications were far weaker. It is structurally incompatible with a fixed 0.5-2R target table. This is already covered by the VWAP hunt.

MNQ falsification study (Mesfin, arXiv 2605.04004, 5-min RTH Dec 2021 to Aug 2025, expanding walk-forward): 11 of 14 OHLCV intraday families had gross edge < 2 pts. Volume spike / dry-up was null, post-news drift was null after the spike bars, unconditional gap-fill fade was null, and MGC mean reversion failed. That study used a 2-pt friction, while the owner's NQ friction is ~0.7 pt, so families with 0.7-2 pt gross that it discarded are not ruled out here.

In the same study, Asia-session expansion bars reverse right after their close (T -11.5 at bar+1): the move happens inside the bar. Following a big bar at its close is the wrong side. A fade has only ~0.3 pt gross, which is still below costs.

Order flow: in E-mini the order-flow-imbalance price impact dissipates within ~1 second (Takahashi, arXiv 2508.06788, 2025). VPIN forecasts volatility, not direction, and even that is disputed (Andersen-Bondarenko). This agrees with the vault note 'Level 2 says when, not which way': big_print / ddiv / sweep entries on 1-min bars have a low prior.

Reversal vs continuation on big-move days flips with the macro regime: Mesfin's VVG fade won in 2022-23 and the follow won in 2024. A fixed-side card cannot follow that. Run both sides as separate cards and read them per year.

Gold's strongest post-2020 session effect is the overnight-up / US-day-down asymmetry (Blose-Gondhalekar-Kort JEF 2018; WGC H1 2026: Asia hours +13% vs US hours -15%). It is regime-tied to Asian demand and needs the same-side random check (P4.2s).
The pre-2015 London PM gold-fix informed flow (Caminschi-Heaney JFM 2014: futures in the first minutes predicted the fix 70-80%) predates the 2015 ICE auction reform. Do not assume it survives.

Frequency math: each documented effect fires at most ~1 time a day per market, and NQ and ES legs are ~0.9 correlated. So 5-10 independent trades a day means stacking GC session legs, long/short mirrors and different clock windows, not more NQ/ES copies of one effect.

Open questions to settle with the owner before running: (1) does tod_drift's built-in 6-bar time exit count as allowed under the fixed hm40 exit table; (2) can GC eve-session legs trade live, given the evening Desk sessions are shadow-only; (3) should a time-of-day noise-band block (the paper's 14-day sigma by clock time, gap-adjusted) be built, or should the flat k x daily ATR proxy stand; (4) is a one-sided clock card (GC short/long drift) acceptable under 'edge must make sense'.

ideas.title: VWAP first-touch pullback, trend days only (09:30 VWAP + efficiency-ratio gate)
ideas.effect: On a day that has trended away from the 09:30 VWAP, the first return to VWAP is where late sellers and dip buyers meet the institutions that benchmark to VWAP. The practitioner rule says to trade it only when price has held one side for 30-60 min and VWAP is sloped. An efficiency-ratio gate stands in for 'trend day' and drops range days, which is where VWAP touches fail.
ideas.evidence: Practitioner rule (eltraderfinanciado VWAP guide, https://www.eltraderfinanciado.com/nl/blog/vwap-trading): price on one side of a sloped VWAP for 30-60 min, the first 5-min close back with the trend after a rejection, skip the first 15 min, 09:30-12:00, at most 2 attempts. Its own win table has no sample. Vault 2026-10-13 65%-at-0.75R screen: 'NQ 09:30-12:55 VWAP trend pullback' (5m, 30 min on one side, 2 ATR) gave 61.0% at 0.75R (break-even 57.1%), +$115, t 2.6, 0.66 a day, build days only. The best VWAP lead on file, owner_vwap_pullback_c15, is the same idea (walk-forward +$20k but stood aside in 6 of 15 months).

ideas.title: Raschke 'Holy Grail': ADX-strong trend, first tag of EMA20
ideas.effect: In a strong intraday trend (ADX high), the first pullback to the 20 EMA is a with-trend continuation: trapped counter-trend traders plus trend re-entries. A published rule with one context filter that the library never tried (the library ran ema_pullback with no ADX).
ideas.evidence: Raschke & Connors, Street Smarts (1995): ADX(14) > 30 and rising, price pulls back to the 20 EMA, buy-stop above the high of the touch bar (rule as restated in TradingView scripts, e.g. https://my.tradingview.com/script/hawl3ybg-Holy-Grail-Setup-with-Confidence-Opacity). No audited futures backtest found. Library 2026-10-04, naked ema_pullback: heat map passed on 11 of 23 NQ units, 0 of 23 ES, 0 of 23 GC. Vault 0.75R screen: EMA pullback at most ~60%. The SSRN gold EMA50/VWAP pullback did not replicate on GC (PF 1.10).

ideas.title: VWAP sigma-band breakout with the trend (noise-boundary momentum)
ideas.effect: A close that crosses beyond VWAP +/- k sigma marks a supply/demand imbalance (a trend day), not noise. Joining it captures intraday momentum. This is the momentum twin of the fades, which lose everywhere.
ideas.evidence: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon, 'Beat the Market' (SPY 2007-2024): a break of the 14-day noise boundary, entries only on the hour, VWAP as stop, Sharpe 1.33 at $0.0035/sh with no slippage (https://quantifiedstrategies.substack.com/p/systematic-intraday-trend-following). A TradingView replication reports weaker returns. Vault 2026-10-13: nq_ny_vwap_band_go (join a close beyond 1/1.5/2 sigma) was the best NY VWAP card, 63% of boxes, $36 a trade, passed 2.1 and failed 2.2. Counter-evidence: a DAX VWAP 2-sigma FADE lost with PF 0.64 at 59% wins against a 62.5% break-even (https://backtrex.com/en/backtests/vwap-band-fade-dax).
ideas.family_mapping: ind_signal ind=vwap_dev, mode=follow, edge=enter (an event when (close - session VWAP)/sigma crosses above +lvl = long, below -lvl = short). Open layer: w_start=10:00 (the paper ignores the first half hour); limits max_tr=2.

Most of the money sat in no-target/wide-stop boxes, while the fixed heat map's small-target cells average about zero.

ideas.title: EMA 8/21/55 stack on the VWAP side (the practitioner 'EMA 9/21 + VWAP' rule)
ideas.effect: Practitioners trade EMA crosses only on the VWAP side (longs above, shorts below), so the short-term trend agrees with the day's volume-weighted fair price. The ribbon stack is the cleanest engine form and the only EMA family with some ES/GC support.
ideas.evidence: Many stated-rule scripts (e.g. EMA 9/21 + VWAP slope filter, https://it.tradingview.com/script/2dvhxn9p-EMA-VWAP-Strategy), none with published stats. Against it: vwap_ema_x passed 0/21 NQ units; nq_ny_vwap_cross averaged $19; EMA 9/21 cross peaked at 61% at 0.75R in the 2026-10-13 screen.

ideas.title: Supertrend flip with an ADX trend gate
ideas.effect: Volatility-scaled trend following: a Supertrend(10,3) flip marks a change in short-term trend. Practitioners only take flips when ADX says the market is trending, which cuts the chop whipsaws that kill naked flips.
ideas.evidence: Olivier Seban's Supertrend(10,3) is a widely published stated rule; no audited futures stats found. Library naked supertrend heat map: 9/27 NQ, 4/27 ES, 2/27 GC units passed (the broadest cross-market support of any trend family). Luck count 2026-10-17: supertrend 8 ideas, 2 read, 2 passed (retired single read). Forward check: nq_supertrend_nyam_short 3 trades, -$922 (too few to judge).

NQ 30m afternoon passed BUILD (t 3.18) but failed 2024 (53%).

ideas.title: Squeeze release in the momentum direction (Carter TTM Squeeze)
ideas.effect: Volatility compression (Bollinger inside Keltner) is followed by expansion. Entering at the release with momentum catches the start of the expansion leg, which matches the vault's 'momentum after quiet' lead.
ideas.evidence: John Carter, Mastering the Trade: BB(20,2) inside KC(20,1.5) = squeeze; the trade fires when the bands leave the channel, direction from the momentum histogram. No reliable published win rate (https://therighttrader.com/learn/indicators/ttm-squeeze); the 75% claims are marketing. Library naked squeeze heat map: 4/28 NQ, 0 ES, 1 GC. Vault 2026-10-13 screen: momentum after a quiet prior day (Keltner/Donchian break, ADX) reached 58-59% at 0.75R, +$55-64, t 2.1-2.6, in NQ mornings.

ideas.title: Anchored VWAP from the overnight high/low: reclaim with volume (Shannon AVWAP)
ideas.effect: A VWAP anchored at the overnight extreme is the average cost of everyone who traded since that turn. A volume-backed close back across it puts that group in profit and flips control (Shannon's 'reclaim'). Requiring the 09:30 VWAP to agree adds a second anchor.
ideas.evidence: Brian Shannon's AVWAP doctrine (Benzinga 2022, https://benzinga.com/z/27200039; the 'VWAP hand-off' script https://www.tradingview.com/script/9wtLN3Mf-Anchored-VWAP-Hand-Off/): stated logic, no stats. The new avwap_flip block (2026-10-20) has onh/onl lines, but the library only ran lines rth/globex/week and vol_m 0/1. Vault: plain VWAP-cross ideas on NQ NY averaged $15 (2026-10-13).

ideas.title: Connors RSI(2) dip inside an intraday trend (with-trend mean reversion)

Daily Nasdaq-100 2016-26: 65 trades, 75% win, PF 1.55 (https://backtrex.com/en/backtests/connors-rsi-2-nasdaq-100). That is daily only; no audited intraday futures test found. ideas.title: Gold: Asia-range breakout into the London open, entered on a close
ideas.effect: Gold's Asian session builds a range on thin volume. The European physical/OTC open brings the day's first real flow, and the break of the Asian range tends to run. The mechanism is gold-specific, so it is not the NQ London idea that already failed.
ideas.evidence: MQL5 study, 3.7 years of real-tick MT5 data on XAUUSD (https://www.mql5.com/en/blogs/post/777540): range 03:00-08:00 server time (GMT offset not stated, ~20:00-01:00 ET on a GMT+3 server), OCO stops at 08:00 server, stop at the other side capped at 0.6%, 2.5R target, break-even at 1.5R, skip ranges <0.3% or >1.6% of price. 715 trades, ~49% win, PF 1.38 / 1.37 on two brokers, held-out 2026 PF 1.61 on 157 trades. What did not work: stops inside the range, no range filter, a 5R target. Vault: London/Asia ideas on NQ lose about their costs (2026-10-13), so this is GC-only.

Vault 2026-10-13: the NY opening-range retest was the best NY card ($38, 59% of boxes; 15m 67%), but rvol/htf filters made it worse.

lessons: Published intraday rules have gross edges about the size of their costs. The Zarattini 5-min ORB replicated on NQ at +0.13R gross and +0.002R net, with 4 of 5 indices negative (mql5 776235). The Zarattini QQQ VWAP flip breaks even below ~1 bp a round trip (QuantConnect reproduction). A DAX VWAP 2-sigma fade lost at PF 0.64 with 59% wins against a 62.5% break-even.

Cost per R differs ~4x by market at typical stops: NQ $14 on a 25-pt stop ($500) = 2.8% of R; ES $29 on 5 pts ($250) = 11.6%; GC $24 on 3 pts ($300) = 8%. At 1:1 the break-even is ~51.4% on NQ but ~55.8% on ES. ES/GC legs need fat stops, and their 0.5x ATR cells will drag the heat-map average.

The overnight drift (long 02:00-03:00 ET; Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan) has averaged ~0 since 2021 on ES and NQ (NY Fed Liberty Street, 'The Disappearing Overnight Drift', Jul 2026). The vault's 61% at 0.75R for 02:05 longs is an exit shape, so do not build tod_drift 02:00.

Market intraday momentum (last 30 min follows the day) was already NOT replicated on ES/NQ 2021-08..2024-12 (burned-data ledger 2026-09-20). Grimes' opening-print fade averages 0.75-1.0 ES pt, below costs, and nq_open_fade had 12.5% of boxes profitable. Both are dead.

The library (2026-10-04) tested families NAKED. Practitioner rules are an entry plus one context filter (ADX>30, VWAP side, trend day, momentum agreeing). Today the open-layer gate is the only way to express that context, so most new ideas = family + one fixed gate.

Gates restart at 00:00 ET (18:00 for eve). Nothing can see a prior day, so no 'quiet prior day', no 200-day MA and no multi-day ATR rank. Keep g_n within the bars since midnight; for example, EMA50 on 5m stands in for Connors' 200-day MA.
vol_spike_break's 20-bar median at 09:30 is made of thin pre-market bars, so every opening break passes the volume test. Set w_start >= 10:00, or it is just an ORB.

Families that rest orders on both sides (orb, ib, ib_n, ib_touch, lon_break, straddle, win_bracket, squeeze nr7/inside) are banned by Apex. Use the close-based single-order forms: orb_close, orb_confirm, win_break, squeeze bbkc.

Cross-market support is rare. In the library heat maps only supertrend, ema_ribbon, donchian, first_bar_mom and vol_spike_break pass on some ES and GC units; ema_pullback/orb/straddle/tema are NQ-only. A 5-10 a day stack will lean on NQ, and NQ+ES firing on the same signal is one bet, not two. Put real diversification in GC-specific mechanisms (the London Asia-range break).

Frequency must come from stacking several 0.5-1 a day legs on different clocks (nyam / mid / pm / London-GC), not from loosening one rule. Busier versions of one rule have always fallen to break-even (2026-10-20 hunt).

Vendor win-rate claims for VWAP/TTM/London-gold rules (75-99%) give no sample or period. The only web sources here that state rules plus sample size are the MQL5 gold London study, Grimes' ES opening-print study, and the Zarattini papers with their replications.
Several ideas overlap the running VWAP hunt (vwap_touch / avwap_flip / band break / orb_vwap_pb). Read its SELECTION.md before building them twice.

lessons: Nothing on file passes the house law. The only leg that clears Gates 1 and 2 is owner_fvg_oside_15_a1m3_nl_r1: about 1.2 a day, at least 8 walk-forward reads of its family, blind +$6.6k on 99 trades (t 0.8), and -$13.5k from May to Aug 2026. The 2026-10-20 hunt went 19 sheets to 3 build passes to 0 of 6 walk-forwards.

Frequency drags every rule to break-even. Pipeline (46,113 NQ cells): 16.4% at the floor under 0.5 a day, 0.5% at 2-3 a day, 0% at 2-3 a day with a target. JJ momentum: 2.4 to 3.1 to 5.1 a day gave +$34 / +$23 / +$12 build and +$42 / +$16 / +$4 walk-forward. None of the 51 taught sheets that trade 2+ a day reaches +0.075R. So 5-10 a day has to come from 5-10 separate legs of about 1 a day each.

Widening a window or adding trades kills the edge. Displacement k1.0 10:00-11:00 $90 became $19 all day; the k1.5 all-day extra trades were worth about $0. Trade 2 of the day pays, trade 3 is about -$11 (cap 2). Candle-break trade 2 went from +$100 build to -$103 unseen.

Fades lose (share profitable 0.24 vs continuation 0.47; taught fade centres 9%). Same-trigger pairs: displacement follow $54.5 vs fade -$49.9; OR close $24 vs fade -$37; candle break $50 vs sweep -$10 to -$36; open-side FVG $98 vs disp_oside 52 of 52 losing. The only fade that held is pdsweep at 0.19 a day.

Stop width decides the sign. Stops of 20 pts or less, wick stops and 1-5m candle stops lose. 30-110 pt stops (3x 1-min ATR, a 15m candle) work. Example: the 09:31 candle with a 100 pt stop made +$67k, with 25 pts -$85k. On hm40, avoid the 0.5x cells on 1m/5m bars.

Win rate is exit geometry. Random entries win 64-66% at 0.5R, and every '70% win' box is a 0.5R box; all 4 failed unseen. 1R is the peak for structure stops (displacement 0.75R $88 / 1R $177 / 1.25R $140). The target in points needs to be at least about 35-40.

Mid-2025 regime change. All three best build-day NQ rules (FVG, 10:00 displacement, 13:30 bar) failed or were thin in their walk-forwards. The hunt's build passes made their money in months the blocks never test and lost the blind months. The hour-of-day bias flipped in 2025. am_fvg15_gap died Jul-Oct 2026. The reverse also happened: the tight 09:30 straddle was 0/17 build and 16/16 unseen, and the 20:00 candle flipped sign.

NQ only. ES: 22% of cells profitable, 1 of 83 maps passes. GC: 0 floor cells in 16,848. Both leaders fail on ES and GC. Every NQ build edge that also lost on ES or GC was later noise unseen, so treat that as a red flag.

Sessions: pm (3.5-5.5x random lift) and mid (2.2-2.6x) are where maps beat random entries. A green 1m/5m nyam map is drift. London is 0 of 15 maps, Asia 0 of 7, the evening has none; the 03:00 candle is the only exception. First-bar follow works at 09:30 and 13:30, not at 11:00 or 03:00.

Filters lift the fit, not the check. Simplicity ladder PF: R0 0.96 / 0.97, R1 1.06 / 0.99, R2 1.32 / 0.96 (FIT / CHECK). Day filters failed 6 of 6 hold-outs. VWAP and EMA side filters on breakouts hurt. Three filtered round-2 locks collapsed (PF 1.27 to 0.74 and so on). The one recurring helpful gate is a day-context side built into the trigger: the 09:30-open side, the overnight-range third, or the 01:00 VWAP.

Long-only build passes are drift (Conti long beat random longs 0%), and short-only failed every unseen read. P4.2s is required for one-sided rules, but it is biased against side-picking rules because it draws random trades only on fire days.

The blind months are nearly used up. Test months are always Jan / May / Sep, and the only never-built ones are 2025-09, 2026-01 and 2026-05 (about 63 weekdays). 31 walk-forwards have read them, so a new pass now is about 3:1 luck. The next fresh month is Jan 2027, so treat any new pass as weak.

The per-block monthly pick added nothing (the candle-break pick changed 13 of 14 times; eve_2000 15 of 15). It made 0.6-a-day rules stand aside and fail on count (displacement 130 test trades, 13:30 bar 165). The fixed-box route fixes this: the displacement's fixed 1R cell made $123 on 188 trades where the pick failed.

Calibration of evidence: a build-day pass holds unseen about 1 time in 5-10. A heat map over 60% green is profitable the next year 48% of the time (base rate 27%). Luck alone gave up to 7.4 of 22 pipeline unseen 'passes'. The 9 locked boxes on 18 fresh sessions: 0 beat 95% of random.
Fat tails: winners with no target lose without their best 5% of trades (donch -$111k, displace -$129k). The hm40 2R cap removes the 3R / no-target geometry that the 03:00 candle and onr_orb used.

Tooling traps to check before any run: candle930 med_m / vol_m+sec and orb_close vwap read past tapes through the build seal, so they cannot be walk-forwarded. win_candle / win_break / win_bracket cannot be sheeted outside nyam (taught.py about line 538). nq_onr_break_a15 failed its code check. The NQV0 1m file is not roll-adjusted, which corrupts 18:00-anchored VWAPs and ATRs. asia2000 was a look-ahead. jj_fair's struct stop had a 3-pt bug (now fixed). noise_band, straddle and ind_signal have no structure level, so they get 20 ATR cells only.

Realistic portfolio math: the 12 ideas add up to about 8 a day only if all pass. On past pass rates of 1 in 5-10, expect 2-3 legs and about 2-3 a day, so the 5-10 a day target is not supported by anything on file.

ideas.title: ES intraday momentum noise band
ideas.effect: When SPY/ES moves beyond its usual intraday noise range from the open and holds on the right side of VWAP, the move tends to continue for the rest of the session. The proposed mechanism is dealer gamma and leveraged-ETF hedging.
ideas.evidence: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon 2024, 'Beat the Market' (SPY, 2007 to 2024): noise area = open ± average absolute move over 14 days, checked every half hour; reported 19.6% a year, Sharpe 1.33 net (authors' own numbers). Baltussen et al., JFE 2021: market intraday momentum across 60+ futures, strongest in equity indexes. Gao et al. (JFE 2018) find the same on SPY. Vault: the NQ PM day-move follow is the one four-windows rule that held unseen (59.4%, PF 1.20).

The cousin vault_break (01:00 anchor) lost its blind months on NQ (-$5.0k). The paper is long-horizon; 2021-2026 alone may be thin. Trend followers win 30-45% at higher R, so judge against break-even + 3 points.

ideas.title: ES late-day momentum (follow the day's move at ~15:00)
ideas.effect: The return from the open (or the prior close) to mid-afternoon predicts the return into the close, because hedgers rebalance in the same direction late in the day.
ideas.evidence: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018, SPY 1993-2013): the first half-hour predicts the last half-hour, more so on volatile, high-volume and news days. Baltussen et al. (JFE 2021): the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes in 60+ futures. Vault 2026-10-14: NQ, follow the day's move at 15:00 when |move| ≥ 0.5 x prior range. Build: 62%, PF 1.28. Unseen: 59.4%, PF 1.20, +$10k. The 15:30 version LOST and 14:30 was weaker, so use ~15:00.

ideas.effect: Gold's main US session settles at 13:30 ET. If market intraday momentum holds for commodities, the day's return so far (from the 08:20 COMEX open or the prior close) should predict the last half-hour before the 13:30 settlement, not the 16:00 equity close.
ideas.evidence: Baltussen et al. (JFE 2021): rest-of-day returns predict the last 30 minutes across equity, bond, commodity and FX futures. A commodity-futures paper (Hull repository) finds the first half-hour predicts the last half-hour in all four commodities it studied. A Chinese gold-futures paper finds the first half-hour of the session that carries the US news predicts the rest. No COMEX-specific study was found. Vault: GC's hour table is mixed; the one significant GC hour is 16-17 ET, after the flat.

ideas.effect: Gold tends to rise during Asian hours (Chinese and Indian physical buying) and to sell off during US hours: a 'hat-shaped' day.

Donati & Jung (CBS thesis): robust appreciation in eastern hours and depreciation the rest of the day, with drops around the London fix. Vault 2026-10-13: the strongest GC/SI/ES clock half-hours cluster at 16:30-18:30 ET. But the vault hour table (build days) found no Asian hour on GC that clears luck.

Thin evening liquidity means wide fills.

ideas.title: ES night VWAP z-fade
ideas.effect: In the thin overnight book, price stretched far from VWAP is mostly liquidity demand, not information. Liquidity providers are paid for fading it, and the short-term reversal premium is larger when liquidity is scarce.
ideas.evidence: Nagel, 'Evaporating Liquidity' (RFS 2012): reversal returns proxy the return to liquidity provision and rise when liquidity is scarce. Dai, Medhat, Novy-Marx & Rizova (2023): lower turnover gives more persistent, stronger reversals. Vault 2026-10-13: the 18:00-01:55 frontier tops out at 58.9% at 0.75R and ≥1 a day (NQ and others), and EVE fade families on NQ had median PF 0.82-0.91. ES at night has never been run on this route.

ideas.title: GC Asia-open (20:00 ET) candle follow
ideas.effect: The Shanghai Gold Exchange day open (09:00 Beijing = 20:00 ET in US winter, 21:00 in summer) and the Tokyo morning bring the eastern physical buyers. A strong first candle may set the evening's direction.
ideas.evidence: Asia-hours appreciation (WGC 2026; Donati & Jung). Vault 2026-10-11: the NQ 20:00 candle (body ≥ 0.7) held its test-days read (PF 1.20, 73 trades) but lost on build days, so the sign flipped, likely a regime. The NQ 18:00 candle failed out of sample. GC never tested.
ideas.family_mapping: open_candle, start = 2000, followed at its close, tf 5 (neighbor 15).
ideas.needs_new_block: no (open_candle home-session check, as for 03:00). A DST-aware 'SGE open' start would need a new block.
ideas.risk: China has no DST, so for ~8 months the SGE open is 21:00 ET, not 20:00. The NQ result flipped sign between periods. Thin evening liquidity. It overlaps the GC evening drift idea; take one.

ideas.title: ES European-open overnight drift (02:00-03:00 long)
ideas.effect: Index futures rose in the hour of the European open, mostly after heavy selling into the prior US close: dealers unload inventory when Europe arrives.
ideas.evidence: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan (RFS 2023): 02:00-03:00 ET carried more than 60% of the ES close-to-close return over 1998-2020, much more after net selling at the close. BUT the NY Fed's Liberty Street post (Jul 2026) finds the window flat over 2021-2025 in ES, NQ and YM, because closing-imbalance dispersion fell from 6.5% to 2.9%. Vault: the NQ 02:05 long (4 ATR, 0.75R) was 61.3% on build days and failed unseen (58.5%, PF 1.08). After a down US session it was 62.7% on build days (0.46 a day).
ideas.family_mapping: tod_drift, dir LONG, home asia, tf 15 (exit at the 03:00 session end).
ideas.per_day: ~1.0 (or ~0.45 with the down-close condition)
ideas.needs_new_block: no for the plain version. Yes for the documented conditional: a day rule 'prior US session closed down / heavy closing imbalance' does not exist (roc gate on bars is only a rough proxy).
ideas.risk: Low priority: the effect is reported dead since 2021, which is the whole data range here, and the NQ unseen read failed. The 1-hour hold caps targets. Include only to close the question, or as the conditional version if a block is built.

lessons: Only scheduled-release brackets on GC (08:30 and 10:00) have beaten the random-entry controls on file. Non-release 08:30 days lost -$6.6k, so the release is the edge, not the clock time. Straddle clock times on ES and GC passed at no time.

ES fails nearly everywhere on file: library stage 1, all ES cards in the first 46 pipeline ideas, 15m candle break -$34k, the 09:31 candle (12 of 16 cells lose), AM VWAP pullback PF 0.84, evening VWAP pullback PF 0.75 with all 5 years negative. NQ rules do not port to ES/GC, so ES/GC ideas need their own mechanism.

Night sessions: London and NY liquidity sweeps are dead on NQ. The 18:00 NQ candle failed out of sample (PF 0.68). The 20:00 candle held out of sample but had lost on build days (sign flip = regime). The 03:00 candle is the only night rule that held its read (PF 1.26).
Overnight drift: the NQ 02:05 long failed unseen (58.5%, PF 1.08). The NY Fed (Liberty Street, Jul 2026) reports the 02:00-03:00 window flat 2021-2025 in ES, NQ and YM, which is all of our data.

Look-ahead trap: the liq level asia2000 inside the eve session read the same evening's future 20:00-24:00 range (a fake 88.8% win, t 12). Avoid liq levels=all/asia2000 in eve unless that is confirmed fixed.

Hour-of-day: ES 10-11 down / 11-12 up flipped in 2025, and every standout hour loses without its best 5% of trades. GC's only significant hour is 16-17 ET (t 4.5), after the 15:58 flat. GC/SI/ES clock drift clusters at 16:30-18:30 ET.

NQ-ES lead-lag is not worth a new block: 1-minute cross-market correlations ≤ 0.03, and the SMT-divergence fade had a median of 55% (best 59%). 'smt' is a menu filter and is not usable on this route anyway.

Late-day momentum: the NQ follow of the day's move at 15:00 is the one four-windows rule that held unseen (59.4%, PF 1.20). The textbook 15:30 version lost and 14:30 was weaker, so use ~15:00, inside the 15:58 flat.
Bracket families (orb, straddle, win_bracket): the main setting must act when the orders are placed (offset, range length, day rule). A w_end after placement is a no-op: 48 'variants' were 12 boxes.

Costs at night: ES/GC night 5-min ATRs are a few points or ticks, so the $29 (ES) and $24 (GC) round turns eat 20-40% of a 1-ATR stop. Prefer 15/30-min bars or 1.5-2 ATR cells. Floors: ES $75, GC $140 a trade.

Data: the 1-min NQ file is not roll-adjusted (+81..+278 pt jumps at 19:00/20:00 ET on ~11 sessions), which corrupts 18:00-anchored VWAP and ATR in EVE/LDN screens. The tick tester uses one contract per session and is not affected.

Filters overfit: each added rule lifted build PF (+0.10, then +0.26) while the check period moved +0.03 / -0.03. Keep one main setting and no filters. One-sided clock rules must pass the same-side random check (P4.2s).

Blind months: the block walk-forward's test months (Jan/May/Sep) have been read by ~31 walk-forwards, mostly NQ. ES/GC boxes are probably a cleaner out-of-sample test than more NQ, but check the ledger before claiming so.

Prop-sim 'one-win size': the 03:00/18:00/20:00 candle eval odds jump to ~39% at the size where one 3R win clears the target. That is a sizing artifact, not edge; do not read it as the strategy getting better.
